note: Each skill path is relative to this package directory (orca-project-delivery), for example skills\code-review\SKILL.md resolves to <package-root>\skills\code-review\SKILL.md.

skills.name: game-design
skills.description: Define and evaluate a game's core loop, choices, rules, feedback, and progression through playable hypotheses. Use when designing a game, specifying a gameplay feature, or diagnosing an unclear or unrewarding play loop.

skills.name: game-economy-design
skills.description: Model resource flows, progression costs, purchases, and reward incentives with explicit balance tests. Use when designing currencies, shops, crafting, upgrades, or currency rewards from ads or purchases.

skills.name: game-level-design
skills.description: Design playable spaces and challenge sequences using movement metrics, reachability, teaching order, and failure data. Use when creating or reviewing levels, rooms, encounters, waves, tracks, or difficulty ramps.

skills.name: game-3c-design
skills.description: Co-design Character, Controller, and Camera behavior as a measurable perception-and-action system. Use when specifying movement, aiming, traversal, animation response, camera transitions, or diagnosing inconsistent game feel.

skills.name: gameplay-programming
skills.description: Structure game rules, behavior decisions, action input, and versioned saves around testable simulation boundaries. Use when implementing gameplay, NPC decisions, responsive controls, or save migration.

skills.name: game-physics
skills.description: Diagnose unstable motion through simulation timing, interpolation, collision coverage, and contact budgets. Use when game objects jitter, tunnel, bounce unpredictably, or behave differently across render rates.

skills.name: game-content-pipeline
skills.description: Define reproducible conversion from authored game content to compatible runtime data with stable identity and incremental updates. Use when building import rules, content catalogs, generated levels, or content update validation.

skills.name: game-performance
skills.description: Identify the limiting game workload and measure one targeted improvement at a time against frame and memory budgets. Use when a game drops frames, hitches, exceeds device budgets, or needs a defensible optimization decision.

skills.name: game-multiplayer
skills.description: Choose multiplayer authority and synchronization models with testable simulation, latency, and recovery contracts. Use when designing state replication, input synchronization, prediction, rollback, or lag compensation.

skills.name: engine-urhox
skills.description: Develop UrhoX games within TapTap Maker using project-pulled documentation and local, remote, and device verification. Use when the delivery target is a TapTap Creative Workshop game.

skills.name: engine-cocos-creator
skills.description: Choose and verify Cocos Creator delivery paths across mini-games, native targets, and Web using official platform and tooling boundaries. Use when building, previewing, or exporting a Cocos Creator game.

skills.name: engine-unity
skills.description: Select and validate Unity projects with separate global Unity and Tuanjie platform, tooling, and license paths. Use when developing a C# game in Unity or assessing Unity for a target channel.

skills.name: engine-godot
skills.description: Select and verify Godot projects using version-matched documentation, export presets, and explicit platform and tooling limits. Use when building, previewing, or exporting a Godot game.

skills.name: engine-unreal
skills.description: Plan Unreal projects around target packaging, Blueprint and C++ boundaries, experimental tooling, and pinned royalty terms. Use when developing an Unreal game or evaluating Unreal for a target device.

skills.name: engine-web-canvas
skills.description: Choose and verify browser-first games built with Phaser or native Canvas while keeping wrapper, channel, and cloud-service boundaries explicit. Use when building or exporting a JavaScript or TypeScript browser game.

skills.name: game-asset-pipeline
skills.description: Plan and validate game assets from type selection through generation or import, postprocessing, and engine intake while preserving identity and provenance. Use when producing, replacing, or accepting a game asset family.

skills.name: game-audio
skills.description: Design game sound as a mixing graph and a responsive music system with measured gain, ducking, variation, and timing. Use when balancing game audio, adding adaptive music, or diagnosing masking and repetitive effects.

skills.name: game-testing-ladders
skills.description: Build a game verification ladder from offline smoke through story, regression, soak, real-device, and certification checks with explicit evidence limits. Use when planning game tests, validating a fix, or assessing release readiness.

skills.name: game-publishing
skills.description: Assess game release readiness across stores, mini-game platforms, and self-hosted web distribution with dated policy checks. Use when selecting a release surface or preparing any game content update for publication.

skills.name: game-build-release
skills.description: Define reproducible game builds, release candidates, gold masters, patches, and rollback decisions across engines. Use when preparing a game build or planning a release update.

skills.name: game-live-ops
skills.description: Plan game seasons, events, economy monitoring, and recovery using player cohorts and operational capacity. Use when operating a released game or designing a repeatable content cadence.

skills.name: game-monetization-iaa
skills.description: Design intent-based game ad placements and economy-sized rewards with measurable player-experience guardrails. Use when adding or evaluating in-app advertising in a game.

skills.name: game-monetization-iap
skills.description: Design game purchase catalogs, first-purchase offers, revenue measurement, and entitlement/refund duties. Use when planning or evaluating in-app purchases and subscriptions.

skills.name: Codebase Reconnaissance
skills.description: Inspect a codebase, branch, history, configuration, and tests to answer scoped factual questions without modifying source. Use for dynamic reconnaissance before planning or review.

skills.name: Technical Research
skills.description: Research current technical behavior using primary sources, source code, standards, and reproducible experiments. Use when library, CLI, protocol, platform, or vendor behavior can affect a decision.

skills.name: Product Discovery
skills.description: Turn a vague product request into a validated problem, users, outcomes, scope, non-goals, assumptions, and acceptance direction. Use before requirements when product intent is unclear.

skills.name: Product Design
skills.description: Design user flows, information architecture, interaction states, accessibility behavior, and testable UX acceptance. Use for UI, workflow, or interaction-heavy tasks.

skills.name: Requirements Analysis
skills.description: Convert objectives and evidence into traceable, unambiguous, testable functional and non-functional requirements. Use before planning or when acceptance is unclear.

skills.name: Solution Architecture
skills.description: Design minimal software boundaries, responsibilities, interfaces, data flow, migration, rollback, and operational behavior for a scoped objective. Use for cross-module or high-risk changes.

skills.name: API Design
skills.description: Design stable HTTP, RPC, event, CLI, or module contracts with validation, errors, idempotency, auth, compatibility, and contract tests. Use when interfaces change.

skills.name: Database Design
skills.description: Design data models, constraints, migrations, transactions, indexes, query patterns, retention, and rollback. Use for schema or persistence changes.

skills.name: Implementation Planning
skills.description: Turn an approved requirement and design into small, self-contained, dependency-aware Tasks with exact scope, acceptance, tests, roles, skills, branches, and reports.

skills.name: Test-Driven Development
skills.description: Use RED-GREEN-REFACTOR to implement behavior with evidence. Use for source changes where a focused automated test can express the intended contract.

skills.name: Systematic Debugging
skills.description: Reproduce, isolate, explain, fix, and verify defects through evidence-driven hypothesis testing. Use for bugs, flaky behavior, regressions, and unexplained failures.

skills.name: Code Review
skills.description: Perform independent, evidence-based review for spec compliance, correctness, lifecycle, concurrency, error handling, maintainability, and test quality. Use before integration.

skills.name: Security Review
skills.description: Review trust boundaries, authentication, authorization, input handling, secrets, sensitive data, injection, dependencies, configuration, and abuse paths. Use for security-sensitive changes.

skills.name: Performance Review
skills.description: Measure and analyze latency, throughput, complexity, queries, memory, concurrency, caching, and capacity. Use for performance-sensitive code or claimed optimizations.

skills.name: Integration Verification
skills.description: Verify Task and final-delivery acceptance with commands, runtime evidence, integration checks, and explicit skipped items. Use before completion claims and final delivery.

skills.name: Merge Conflict Resolution
skills.description: Resolve Git merge conflicts using branch intent, common base, commit history, interfaces, and tests. Use when integrating reviewed work into the delivery branch.

skills.name: Frontend Visual Design
skills.description: Choose typography, color, spacing, and visual hierarchy for an interface. Use when a screen needs a visual specification rather than only a user flow.

skills.name: Browser End-to-End Testing
skills.description: Design and execute browser journeys through the real entry point, including failure paths and retained traces. Use for browser regression evidence. The local example requires Python Playwright and an installed Chromium executable; it reports missing prerequisites by name.

skills.name: Accessibility Audit
skills.description: Audit keyboard access, names, errors, contrast, and reflow, separating tool output from human checks. Use before claiming accessibility conformance.

skills.name: PostgreSQL Practices
skills.description: Choose PostgreSQL indexes, query plans, constraints, and row-level access from measured behavior. Use for PostgreSQL schema or query work.

skills.name: Observability
skills.description: Design logs, metrics, and traces that identify a failed unit from evidence. Use when adding or reviewing operational instrumentation.

skills.name: CI Pipeline
skills.description: Design deterministic CI stages, failure gates, and artifact retention. Use when changing a pipeline or diagnosing why a check did not block delivery.

skills.name: React Performance
skills.description: Measure and reduce React request waterfalls, rendering cost, and bundle weight without changing behavior. Use for evidenced React performance work.

skills.name: React Composition
skills.description: Compose React state and components explicitly instead of multiplying boolean modes. Use when component APIs or shared state become ambiguous.

skills.name: Icon Assets
skills.description: Select, size, and trace icon assets with source and license records. Use when an interface needs a consistent icon set.

skills.name: SVG Logo Design
skills.description: Design and review scalable SVG marks for legibility, color, and export sizes. Use for a logo delivered as vector artwork.

skills.name: Web Assets
skills.description: Generate a deterministic web icon and manifest size plan from explicit brand inputs. Use for favicon and PWA asset contracts.

skills.name: Image Compression
skills.description: Compress images only when bytes shrink and the decoded image remains valid. Use for deterministic local image optimization.

skills.name: Image Generation
skills.description: Generate and save an OpenAI image with offline fixtures and explicit online opt-in. Use only for an authorized image task.

skills.name: Infographic Design
skills.description: Turn verified quantities into a readable infographic layout and generation brief. Use before rendering a data graphic.

skills.name: Editorial Illustration
skills.description: Plan an editorial illustration that supports one article claim without fabricating evidence. Use for covers and article art briefs.

skills.name: Visual Slide Deck
skills.description: Plan a visual slide sequence and label rendered images as non-editable pictures. Use for image-based decks rather than Office objects.

skills.name: Code Video Production
skills.description: Author and render a local HyperFrames code video with explicit timing and media acceptance commands. Use for HTML-authored code explainers.

skills.name: Generated Video
skills.description: Submit, inspect, and download Pexo video work with offline fixtures and explicit online opt-in. Use for an authorized generated-video task.

api.purpose: Example asynchronous video contract; configuration does not authorize a call

skills.name: Media Transcoding
skills.description: Plan and execute local FFmpeg transcoding with explicit dimensions, frame rate, codecs, and FFprobe acceptance checks.

skills.name: Document Production
skills.description: Produce and reopen Markdown, editable DOCX/PPTX/XLSX, and PDF from structured source using independently written local examples.

skills.name: Design System
skills.description: Define the shared tokens and component contracts a product reuses across screens. Use when more than one screen must share the same type, color, spacing, or component behavior.

skills.name: Domain Modeling
skills.description: Assign entities, value objects, aggregates, and invariants to a bounded context before choosing storage. Use when the domain language is unsettled and no schema change is in scope yet.

skills.name: Localization
skills.description: Prepare source copy so placeholders, plural rules, and right-to-left layout survive translation. Use when shipping text that will be translated or pseudo-localized. Not for writing the translation itself.

skills.name: MCP Server Development
skills.description: Design an MCP server tool surface, classify protocol errors separately from tool errors, and verify the messages against the pinned specification. Use when adding or changing tools on a Model Context Protocol server. Not for HTTP API design.

skills.name: Migration Upgrade
skills.description: Order a dependency, framework, library, or API upgrade so every step ships independently and reverses. Use when a version change must roll out while old and new code both run. Not for designing a new schema.

skills.name: Skill Authoring Evaluation
skills.description: Evaluate a method Skill for triggering, counterexamples, and observable task quality. Use when reviewing or authoring a SKILL.md before registration.

skills.name: Subtitle Production
skills.description: Convert SRT and WebVTT subtitles with validated timing and connect cues to a transcript. Use for local caption files.

skills.name: Technical Diagrams
skills.description: Draw an editable architecture or sequence diagram as SVG or Mermaid with readable type, contained text, and theme-safe contrast. Use when a change needs a diagram maintained beside the text. Not for slide layout or logo design.
